display.purpose: Top of the UI ramp (Material displayMedium, 36px). Asks for Inter 800; no Inter 800 file is bundled.

display-warm.purpose: Hero display for brand moments: login, onboarding, empty states (Material displayLarge, 40px).

headline.purpose: Section and screen headlines (Material headlineMedium); 26px and 18px steps come through the Material mapping.

body.purpose: Default reading text: settings-row titles, input text, body copy (Material bodyLarge, 15px).

caption.purpose: Subtitles, hints and metadata (Material bodySmall and labelMedium, 13px).

link.purpose: Link text: underlined, with the accent colour applied where it is used.

mono.purpose: Inline code and monospace snippets; RobotoMono.

handwriting-display.purpose: Brand wordmark and hero headings; Caveat, with Ma Shan Zheng carrying Chinese.

handwriting-title.purpose: Screen titles in the handwritten voice. Declared; its usage was not in the documented sources.

handwriting-body.purpose: Note titles on note cards: the first line of the note, in both list and grid layouts.

handwriting-note-body.purpose: Handwritten preview text on sticky-note cards.

shadows.name: paper
shadows.purpose: Sticky-note cards in light mode: a warm diffuse layer plus a tight contact layer, so the paper looks placed on a desk. Flutter offset (3,6) blurRadius 16, then offset (1,2) blurRadius 4.

shadows.name: paper-dark
shadows.purpose: Sticky-note cards in dark mode: the same two layers in 12.5% black.

shadows.name: sheet-lift
shadows.purpose: Cast upward by a page while it is being pushed onto the one below it; it moves with the page. Flutter offset (0,-10) blurRadius 28.

shadows.name: card-press
shadows.purpose: Added under a tappable CardContainer while it is pressed. Flutter offset (0,4) blurRadius 12, primary at alpha 12.

shadows.name: sm
shadows.purpose: Declared light-mode step for list cards and compact tiles. Paints nothing: the shadow ink is a six-digit literal, so its alpha is 0.

shadows.name: md
shadows.purpose: Declared light-mode step for prominent cards and list headers. Paints nothing: alpha 0.

shadows.name: lg
shadows.purpose: Declared light-mode step for dialogs and floating panels. Paints nothing: alpha 0.

shadows.name: xl
shadows.purpose: Declared light-mode step for overlays and popovers. Paints nothing: alpha 0.

shadows.name: sm-dark
shadows.purpose: Dark-mode step for list cards and compact tiles.

shadows.name: md-dark
shadows.purpose: Dark-mode step for prominent cards and list headers.

shadows.name: lg-dark
shadows.purpose: Dark-mode step for dialogs and floating panels.

shadows.name: xl-dark
shadows.purpose: Dark-mode step for overlays and popovers.

motion.name: fast
motion.purpose: Immediate feedback: a press, a toggle, an arrow turning, text swapping.

motion.name: standard
motion.purpose: A routine state change: a sheet, a card settling, a tab switch, a fade.

motion.name: expressive
motion.purpose: The one authored move a screen is allowed: a note settling into place. Declared in AppAnimation; no use of it appears in the documented sources.

motion.name: arrive
motion.purpose: Coming into place (Flutter Cubic(0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1)): quick to start, then a long glide to rest, the way a hand puts something down.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Pressing down. Over-damped, so nothing wobbles under a thumb. No CSS equivalent; the web stand-ins approximate it with the arrive curve.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: Letting go. Just short of critical damping, so a thing lands with one small dip past its place and stops; about 450ms to rest. No CSS equivalent.

motion.name: reduce-motion
motion.purpose: The in-app switch 减少动画, as served by context.motion: every duration is zero and every curve is linear, so a move becomes a change of state. Presses dim to 72% opacity instead of scaling; loops do not start.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: FilledButton: the one filled action on a screen. Soft Periwinkle Purple fill, white 15px/600 label, 16px corners, 14x24 padding; a press gives to 0.97 scale on the press/settle springs. The hover colour and the focus ring are web stand-ins: the theme leaves hover, focus and pressed colour to Material's defaults.
components.html:
<button class="ds-btn-primary" type="button"><svg class="ds-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="18" height="18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" role="img" aria-label="AppIcons.save"><rect x="5" y="5" width="14" height="14" rx="3"/></svg>Save</button>
<button class="ds-btn-primary" type="button" disabled>Save</button>

components.name: Tonal Button
components.description: FilledButton.tonal: the quieter call to action (empty-state button, retry), 16px corners. Its fill and label are Material's secondaryContainer/onSecondaryContainer, derived from the seed and not pinned to a token; Lavender Tint and Deep Accent Purple are stand-ins for them. Hover and focus are web stand-ins.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-tonal" type="button"><svg class="ds-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="18" height="18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" role="img" aria-label="AppIcons.add"><rect x="5" y="5" width="14" height="14" rx="3"/></svg>New note</button>

components.name: Text Input
components.description: The themed text field: filled with Warm Input Fill, 1px Warm Border, 16px corners, 14x16 padding, body type. Focus grows the border to 2px in Soft Periwinkle Purple at alpha 120; error draws Error Red. The hover and active borders are web stand-ins (the warm disabled grey as the next darker neutral), and Error Red stands in for the theme's error colour, which Material derives and the theme does not pin.
components.html:
<input class="ds-input-field" type="text" placeholder="Write a note" aria-label="Note">
<input class="ds-input-field" type="text" value="" placeholder="Required" aria-label="Required field" aria-invalid="true">

components.name: Search Field
components.description: Derived stand-in, not a documented widget: the text-input theme with AppIcons.search as a leading glyph. No dedicated search-field widget was among the documented sources, so nothing more specific is known about it. The hover and active borders are web stand-ins.

components.name: Bottom Navigation
components.description: Material 3 NavigationBar theme: Warm Card White, height 56, no elevation, Lavender Tint indicator behind the selected icon, 10px labels. The four destinations use the navigation regular/fill pairs from AppIcons; the filled cut marks the selected one. Geometry the theme does not set (indicator size) is Material's default. Labels are placeholders.

components.name: Chip
components.description: The theme's Chip: Cool Chip Grey pill with a 13px/500 Slate Ink label in light; selected takes Lavender Tint with a Deep Accent Purple label. Dark differs in shape: Navy Input Fill, 1px Navy Border, 12px corners. The tag chips on note cards come from a widget outside the documented sources. Hover and focus are web stand-ins.

components.name: Sticky-Note Card
components.description: The signature component: a note as a Post-it on the desk. One of six paper tones by list position, 12px corners, no border, a two-layer warm shadow, a slight tilt; handwritten title (22px/500), handwritten preview and a muted timestamp, with a decorative doodle bottom-right. Hover and active reuse the card's own ink highlight (alpha 10) and splash (alpha 20). Sample text and the doodle placeholder are illustrative.

components.name: Settings Row
components.description: SettingsItem inside a SettingsGroup: a 20px-cornered card with a 1px Warm Border, rows with a 32px tinted icon circle, body title and caption subtitle, a 0.5px inset divider. A press scales to 0.98 over 120ms under an 8% purple ink splash. The title's on-surface colour and the destructive row's error colour are Material-derived and not pinned; Slate Ink and Error Red are stand-ins.

narrative.overview:
AnyNote's screens are a warm paper desk. A note is not a row in a database: it is a sheet of pastel sticky-note paper, slightly tilted, resting on the desk under a soft warm shadow, with its title and timestamp in handwriting. Around the notes the interface keeps quiet — cream surfaces, warm near-black ink, generous rounded corners, and one soft purple accent that belongs to controls and state. Paper and handwriting are the product's voice; the direction confirmed on 2026-11-24 has the system layer speak the same language, and the owner chose to amplify that personality (视觉方向「放大个性」) rather than restrain it.

The app is phone-first and comfortable rather than dense. Material 3 governs structure, navigation and interaction, spacing sits on a 4 px grid, and corners are large (the radius scale runs 8–28, plus a pill). There are two full themes. Light is the desk itself, with the six paper tones at full strength. Dark is a deep navy where the same six tones survive only as faint washes and the accent lightens to periwinkle so it still reads. Two high-contrast themes (black on white, and the reverse) exist as a separate choice. Motion behaves like paper (动效「更有表现力」): a note lands and settles, a page is lifted onto the desk to open it, a press gives slightly. Four durations, two curves and two springs cover all of it, and "减少动画" calms every bit of it.

The North Star name and the descriptive colour names in this document were derived by the documenter from the direction the owner confirmed on 2026-11-24 and from the code's own token names. The owner has not reviewed them; they are waiting for that review.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper surfaces with one soft purple accent, used for controls and state.
Six pastel sticky-note tones, cycled by list position and tilted like hand-placed paper.
Handwriting for a note's own words; Inter for everything the interface says.
One icon family — Phosphor line (`Regular`), drawn through `AppIcons`.
Paper-like motion from four durations, two curves and two springs; "减少动画" calms all of it.

rules.name: The Accent Is for Controls Rule
rules.body: Purple marks controls and state — buttons, focus, selection, the pin. The six paper tones mark notes. A sticky note takes the accent only for state: its pin and its selection tint.

rules.name: The Six Sheets Rule
rules.body: A sticky note's colour is one of the six paper tones, picked by its position in the list. A note's own colour setting only chooses among those six; any other colour becomes a faint 40-alpha wash.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Inter speaks for the interface; handwriting speaks for the note. Note titles, note timestamps and the preview on a sticky note are handwritten. Buttons, labels, navigation, settings and body copy are Inter.

rules.name: The Handwriting Weight Rule
rules.body: Handwritten styles stay at 500 (titles, captions) or 400 (note body). Heavier weights are not used: the engine's per-glyph fallback was observed to skip Ma Shan Zheng at 600 on Android, which dropped Chinese back to the plain UI font.

rules.name: The Paper Edge Rule
rules.body: A sticky note has no border. Its colour block plus the two-layer warm shadow is the edge.

rules.name: The No Tint Rule
rules.body: Elevation never changes a surface's colour: `surfaceTintColor` is transparent on every themed surface. Depth is shown by shadow or by a 1 px border, never by tint.

dos: Do draw every icon through `AppIcons` — Phosphor `Regular`, one stroke weight — and name it by what it means (`delete`, not `trash`).
Do use `…Filled` only as the on state of a toggle, beside its `Regular` twin.
Do take every duration, curve and spring from `AppAnimation`, and ask `context.motion` for authored motion such as staggers, springs and page transitions.
Do give a sticky note its tone from the six-sheet cycle through `PaperTokens.of(context).toneFor(index, brightness)`; that is also what produces the dark washes.
Do write note titles and note timestamps in the handwriting family, and keep everything the interface says in Inter.
Do take radii from `AppRadius` (16 px for inputs and filled buttons, 20 px for cards, 12 px for sticky notes) and spacing from `AppSpacing`.
Do make "减少动画" calm every new animation: loops do not start, and moves become changes of state.
Do mark decorative drawing as decorative, the way the sticky-note doodle is excluded from semantics.
donts: Don't use Material `Icons.*`, or a Phosphor class anywhere outside `AppIcons`.
Don't use `…Filled` on its own as decoration, or `Bold` outside the two high-contrast theme choices.
Don't declare a duration, curve or spring of your own.
Don't put a border on a sticky note; its colour block and warm shadow are the edge.
Don't set a handwritten style above weight 500.
Don't set UI controls — buttons, navigation, settings rows — in the handwriting family.
Don't tint a surface to show elevation.
Don't hard-code a paper tone for dark mode; resolve it through `toneFor`.
